title: Credit sweep & staggered hiring lattice (working)
content:
Context and purpose:
- Quick working sheet to test an alternative to slab/commit buckets: run a monthly 'credit sweep' that reallocates unused burst credits to a transient hire pool and to token-price smoothing. Use a staggered hiring lattice (small hires + contractors) to retain flexibility.

High-level hypothesis:
- If we allow monthly credit sweep and convert 40% of unused credits into a short-term contractor budget, we reduce permanent HC by 6 FTEs while preserving burst capacity at 95% of current SLA. Tradeoff: higher per-token marginal cost in extreme spikes.

Scenario matrix (summary):
Columns: Scenario | Effective token price delta vs baseline | FTE change by Q2 | Contractor-months budgeted | Expected SLA tail (p99ms) | Estimated monthly burn delta
- Baseline | 0% | +0 | 0 | p99=220ms | $0
- Credit-sweep conservative | +7% | -3 | 210 contractor-months | p99=240ms | +$320k
- Credit-sweep aggressive | +12% | -6 | 420 contractor-months | p99=275ms | +$560k
- Price-shock (demand +50%, no sweep) | -8% (we absorb via reserves) | +8 (fast hires) | 0 | p99=310ms | +$1.1M

Working budget table (month-level slices) - columns described verbally for spreadsheet import:
- Month, Planned new FTEs, Contractor-months, Burst-credit draw (tokens), Token-price (USD/1k), GPU-hour reserve ($), Monthly delta vs baseline ($)
Example rows:
- 2026-11, 0, 35, 25M, 3.6, 120k, +12k
- 2026-12, 1, 25, 30M, 3.8, 140k, +46k
- 2027-01, 2, 75, 45M, 4.1, 200k, +152k
- 2027-02, 1, 60, 40M, 3.9, 180k, +98k

Key assumptions & heuristics (for modeling):
- Unused credits = committed capacity not consumed in prior 30 days. We can legally (contractually) roll these into an internal pool; assume 60% reclaim rate.
- Contractors cost effective multiplier = 1.8x FTE fully-loaded hourly for short contracts (includes onboarding, reduced productivity).
- Each new FTE reduces contractor-months need by 12 months * 0.6 (ramp and focus on ops tasks).
- Token-to-GPU mapping: 1M tokens ~ 0.35 GPU-hours on average mix of models.
- Latency impact: contractor-managed burst scaling increases tail latency by an empirical factor (observed from past incident: 10–25% on p99). We use +10% p99 for conservative, +25% for aggressive.

Price sensitivity sweep (one-pager methodology):
1) Run three levers separately: slab commit change, quantization adoption (5% cost reduction / token at scale), and credit-sweep reallocation.
2) For each lever, compute marginal unit cost curve and elasticity (elasticity measured as change in usage for +1% price change).
3) Run Monte Carlo (n=3k) over demand shock distribution (mu +20%, sigma 18%) to find tail cost exposures and required HC cushion.

Unresolved questions / decision points (notes to self):
- Legal check: confirm ability to convert unused committed credits across customers in multi-tenant contract vs dedicated customers. (Assigned to Oliver)
- Ops checklist: what is ramp time to onboard 1 HC in infra/infra-sre vs platform? Use 3-month full productivity window by default.
- CS impact: will tiered customers notice token-price smoothing (we're implicitly lowering visible per-token price by reallocation)? Need a templated customer note.

Action items (near term):
- [Aisha] Build import-ready CSV and run sensitivity runs for 3 delta bands (+10%, +20%, -10%). Target: run by 2026-11-20.
- [Marcus] Legal check on credit conversion (due 2026-11-18).
- [Lena] Simulate contractor sourcing cost bands (due 2026-11-22).
- [Oliver] Provide historical p99 hit data from last 9 incidents (due 2026-11-19).

Quick reproducible notes for analysts:
- Source model: "token_econ_v2" in /github.com/redwood-inference/cost-models. Use branch: lattice-credit-sweep. CSV headers above. Run ./run_sensitivity.sh --scenarios sweep,shock,baseline --samples 3000.

Slack refs / context threads:
- #finance: thread: "credit-sweep pilot" (link in Confluence-12345)
- #ops: incident-summary Nov 2026 - spike-handling (see linked_artifacts JIRA-FT-908)

Rough qualitative conclusions (working hypothesis):
- A modest credit-sweep plus staggered hiring lattice gives more runway and preserves burst behavior for typical monthly spikes, but increases marginal unit cost for extreme sustained demand. It should be offered as an internal "ops flexibility" policy rather than customer-facing pricing.

Notes to reader: this is a working sheet — lots of inline approximations. Treat the numbers as directional. If this is useful, we'll port the best cases into the canonical pro-forma and attach a sensitivity graph pack.

End of document.
